kid-1-d4.commentary: White stakes a central claim immediately, seizing space and opening diagonals for the queen and dark-squared bishop.

kid-2-nf6.commentary: Black develops the knight to its most active square, controlling e4 and preserving maximum flexibility for Black's pawn structure.

kid-3-c4.commentary: White reinforces the d4 pawn and fights for the d5 square, steering the game toward a Queen's Pawn structure.

kid-4-g6.commentary: The hallmark of the King's Indian — Black prepares to fianchetto the bishop on g7, building a powerful long-diagonal battery.

kid-5-nc3.commentary: White develops the queen's knight, reinforcing the center and preparing to support an e2-e4 advance.

kid-6-bg7.commentary: The fianchettoed bishop on g7 is the backbone of the King's Indian — it radiates energy toward d4 and beyond.

kid-7-e4.commentary: White erects a broad pawn center with d4+e4+c4, controlling key squares. Black will now seek to undermine it.

kid-8-d6.commentary: Black solidifies the center and prevents e4-e5. This prepares the eventual e7-e5 break which is Black's main counter-plan.

kid-9-nf3.commentary: White develops the king's knight, reinforcing the center and preparing to castle kingside.

kid-10-oo.commentary: Black castles kingside, safeguarding the king and activating the rook. This is the critical junction — White now chooses a plan.

kid-11a-be2.commentary: The Classical Variation — White develops quietly and prepares to castle, aiming for a solid positional struggle. The main line continues with ...e5.

kid-12a-e5.commentary: Black strikes back in the center. This is the thematic King's Indian break — now both sides race to attack on their respective wings.

kid-11b-d5.commentary: The Space Attack / Mar del Plata setup — White advances to d5, closing the center and signaling a queenside space advantage. Black must counterattack on the kingside.

kid-12b-ne7.commentary: Black repositions to challenge the d5 pawn and maneuver toward f4 or e5, preparing the classic ...f5-f4 kingside pawn storm.

ck-1-e4.commentary: White seizes the center with the most popular first move. Against the Caro-Kann, White will build a strong pawn center.

ck-2-c6.commentary: The defining move of the Caro-Kann — Black prepares ...d5 while keeping the c8 bishop's diagonal open. A solid, classical approach.

ck-3-d4.commentary: White builds a pawn phalanx in the center. The fight for d5 will be the key strategic battleground.

ck-4-d5.commentary: Black challenges the center immediately, forcing White to define the pawn structure.

ck-5-nc3.commentary: White defends e4 with the knight, developing naturally. This is the Main Line of the Caro-Kann.

ck-6-dxe4.commentary: Black releases the central tension, entering the main theoretical debate. Now White recaptures and the critical branching point occurs.

ck-7-nxe4.commentary: White recaptures, centralizing the knight powerfully on e4. This is the branch node — Black can choose the Classical or Modern system.

ck-8a-bf5.commentary: The Classical Variation — Black develops the light-squared bishop outside the pawn chain before closing with ...e6. White will play Ng3 to harass it.

ck-9a-ng3.commentary: White retreats the knight to a safe square while attacking the bishop, gaining time.

ck-10a-bg6.commentary: Black retreats the bishop to the g6 square where it remains active on the long diagonal and supports a future ...e5.

ck-8b-nd7.commentary: The Modern Variation — Black develops the knight to d7, planning ...Ngf6 to exchange White's strong centralized knight without giving up the bishop.

ck-9b-nf3.commentary: White develops the king's knight, maintaining the central knight on e4 and preparing to castle.

ck-10b-ngf6.commentary: Black develops the other knight, now challenging White's strong knight on e4 and completing development before castling.
